prompts.text: What's the strangest autocorrect mistake you've sent without noticing?
Tell me about a phone notification that arrived at the funniest possible moment.
A keyboard that reads your mind or a phone that never runs out of battery?
Your phone asks to renegotiate its screen-time rules with you. What would it complain about?
People have wildly different definitions of a tidy phone home screen.
A folder full of unnamed screenshots is a perfectly ordinary digital filing system.
Which app do you open out of habit and immediately forget why?
Recall a time a gadget worked perfectly until somebody asked you to demonstrate it.
You must give your Wi-Fi network a new name to amuse the neighbours. What would you choose?
Keep every photo you've taken or keep every voice note you've received?
What's a dream you woke up from feeling genuinely puzzled?
Remember every dream for a week or choose your own background music while you sleep?
Describe a morning when you couldn't tell whether something happened or you'd dreamt it.
Your alarm clock gets a personality review from you. What feedback does it receive?
Morning people and night owls often describe the same hour like two different worlds.
The best weekend luxury is waking up without wondering what time it is.
What's the most creative excuse you've invented for staying in bed a little longer?
Tell me about a day you woke up early and discovered an unexpected benefit.
Your pillow enters a competition for most loyal household companion. What's its speech?
A five-minute nap whenever you want or the ability to fall asleep instantly at bedtime?
Which ordinary sound would make a surprisingly good ringtone?
Tell me about an unexpected noise that interrupted a perfectly serious moment.
A doorbell that imitates a bird or a microwave that plays a short drum solo?
The items in your kitchen form a band. Which one takes the lead vocals?
Some household sounds are comforting only because people grew up hearing them.
A well-timed sound effect can improve almost any harmless joke.
What's a noise from your childhood home you'd recognise immediately?
Recall a moment when everyone went silent because of a sound nobody understood.
You must choose a theme tune for your front door. What would visitors hear?
Hear your footsteps as musical notes or have your laughter sound like applause for a day?
What's the most imaginative game you invented with almost no equipment?
Tell me about making a toy from materials nobody expected to be fun.
Revisit your favourite childhood playground or recreate a classic indoor game?
You're asked to design a game using only paper, two cups and a spoon. What's the objective?
Children often make their own entertainment before adults finish planning an activity.
An improvised game with confusing rules sometimes beats an expensive new one.
Which old childhood competition would you enter again without any practice?
Describe a time you tried to explain a game to someone and realised the rules made no sense.
You get to add one silly event to a school sports day. What would the teams compete in?
Play an old-fashioned guessing game or build something from cardboard?
What's the least practical thing you've ever spent a long time organising?
Arrange books by colour or by how much you enjoyed reading them?
Tell me about cleaning a drawer and finding something you thought was lost forever.
A professional organiser visits your room and interviews your favourite chair. What does it reveal?
Some people remember where everything is, even in a room that looks completely chaotic.
An untidy desk isn't proof that the person using it lacks a plan.
Which item do you consistently put in a sensible place and immediately lose?
Recall finding an important object somewhere so strange you still can't explain it.
You must organise a competition for the most amusing junk drawer. What would the judges score?
A perfectly arranged wardrobe or a desk where every cable stays untangled?
Which local weather condition seems to change your plans most often?
Tell me about dressing for the wrong weather and trying to make it work.
A raincoat with pockets for everything or shoes that never collect dust?
Your umbrella writes a complaint about your habits. What does it say?
People often remember a rainy outing more vividly than a day with perfect weather.
A sudden change of weather is a reasonable excuse to discover a new indoor café.
What's the oddest object you've used to protect yourself from unexpected rain?
Describe a windy day when holding on to your belongings became an adventure.
Your favourite pair of shoes gets to choose the next destination. Where does it insist on going?
A cool cloudy afternoon outside or a sunny morning indoors with the windows open?
What's one piece of clothing you wear far more often than you intended?
A jacket with endless useful pockets or trainers that always look brand new?
Tell me about an outfit you loved in a photograph but would never choose now.
Your wardrobe elects a spokesperson to describe your fashion choices. Which item wins?
The story behind a treasured item of clothing is sometimes funnier than the item itself.
Comfort deserves a place in every personal style guide.
What's a fashion trend you once dismissed and later tried?
Recall a time you dressed for an occasion and misunderstood the dress code.
You have to name a clothing collection after your daily habits. What would the catalogue feature?
Wear only one favourite colour for a week or try a different colour every day?
What's the funniest misunderstanding you've had with a customer service representative?
Tell me about a small shopping error that led to an unexpectedly useful purchase.
A supermarket with live music or a market where vendors tell short stories?
You are hired to design the least stressful checkout queue. What harmless feature would you add?
Everyone seems to have a different strategy for carrying too many shopping bags at once.
Remembering your shopping list without checking it is an underrated achievement.
What's a grocery item you always forget until you get home?
Recall accidentally buying a completely different item from what you intended.
A shop announces an award for the most creative reusable bag. What would yours look like?
Choose all your groceries in five minutes or get an extra ten minutes to browse for fun?
What's a curious little fact you've learnt that rarely fits into normal conversation?
Know the origins of everyday words or know how common objects were invented?
Tell me about learning something from a stranger that sent you down a research rabbit hole.
You have one minute to give a presentation about an ordinary object you love. What do you choose?
A person's favourite facts often reveal what they notice when no one is watching.
Learning something completely unnecessary is a reasonable use of free time.
What's one question you kept asking as a child that adults struggled to answer?
Describe the first time you became fascinated by how an everyday machine worked.
You must invent a new museum exhibit about modern daily life. What goes in the display?
Visit a science museum with interactive exhibits or wander through a local history collection?
What's an ordinary moment you wish came with a replay button?
Tell me about a chance meeting that made an otherwise routine day interesting.
Receive a surprise free afternoon or find a forgotten note from five years ago?
You are asked to nominate your funniest harmless mistake for an annual award. Which one do you enter?
Some of the best stories come from plans that were never especially important.
A day doesn't need a major achievement to give you a good story.
What's a small personal tradition you've invented for no particular reason?
Recall a conversation that started with an odd question and lasted much longer than expected.
Your future self sends you a postcard with only three words on it. What would you hope they say?
Spend an unexpected free hour learning something new or revisiting an old favourite?
